extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs managing reviewer assignments on OpenReview
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Area Chairs on using OpenReview's Edge Browser to browse, sort, search, create, invite, and remove reviewer–paper assignments and manage reviewer loads and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Edge Browser to visualize matches
rubrics_metrics.description: The edge browser visualizes edges, or matches, created by OpenReview's automatic paper matching algorithm; use it to browse, sort, search, and create new assignments between reviewers and papers until you are happy with the assignments generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the edge browser from a link in the Area Chair console (if enabled). All assigned papers appear in a single column on the left and selecting a paper pulls up reviewers in a second column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand reviewer color coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are colored by their relationship to the selected paper: light green = assigned to the selected paper; white = not assigned and no conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the color cues to quickly identify current assignments and non-conflicted reviewers for the selected paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for papers and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You can search for specific papers by paper title or number at the top of the first column; you can search for reviewers by name, email, or profile id at the top of the second column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use searches to rapidly locate the paper or reviewer you want to inspect or modify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sort reviewers by edge attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort the reviewer column by edge types shown, such as Assignment, Aggregate Score, Bid, or Affinity Score, using the 'Order By' dropdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sorting helps prioritize reviewers (e.g., by affinity score or bids) when creating assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: See reviewer workload at-a-glance
rubrics_metrics.description: The second column will show the total number of assignments for the selected reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this information to avoid overloading reviewers and to respect max assignment limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete an assignment using the trash can
rubrics_metrics.description: You can delete an assignment using the trash can button on a certain Reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion removes the reviewer assignment for that paper; no further UI notes are provided but this is the standard removal method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign button: immediate assignment and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the 'Assign' button assigns a reviewer to a paper and notifies them by email. The assignment becomes automatically available in the Reviewer and AC consoles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Assign' when you want to make the assignment effective immediately and inform the reviewer without requiring their acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite Assignment: optional invitation workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Invite Assignment' button (only available if enabled by Program Chairs) sends an invitation to the reviewer with an accept/decline link; the reviewer can then respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Invite' to request confirmation before assigning, to invite reviewers outside the reviewer pool (search by email or profileID), or when respecting custom reviewer load limits is important. Invitations change reviewer status based on response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict detection when inviting or assigning
rubrics_metrics.description: If you try to invite a reviewer who is in conflict with that paper, a banner will alert you with an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system prevents assignment invitations to conflicted reviewers and surfaces an error banner to the AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation response statuses and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer status after an invitation will change according to their response: 'Declined', 'Pending Sign Up', 'Accepted', or 'Conflict Detected'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor these statuses to know whether invited reviewers accepted or declined and to follow up on pending invites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect custom reduced paper loads (Custom Max Papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reviewers have a custom reduced paper load shown as 'Custom Max Papers'. You cannot directly assign a reviewer to more papers than their custom max papers, but you can 'Invite' reviewers if that option is enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use invitations to potentially bypass direct-assignment limits (subject to program policy). Be careful not to overload reviewers beyond their declared limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter to show reviewers below their max load
rubrics_metrics.description: You can filter out reviewers who have met their quota with the checkbox 'Only show reviewers with fewer than max assigned papers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this filter to focus on reviewers who are available for more assignments and to enforce load balancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite external reviewers by email or profileID
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to invite a reviewer from outside the reviewer pool, including another Area Chair, you can search for their email address or profileID in the search bar of the second column and click 'Invite Assignment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same conflict checks apply; external invitees will receive an email and their status will update based on their response.
